previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient, a male with a history of ankylosing spondylitis, hypertension, obstructive sleep apnea, asthma, and severe obesity, was admitted for acute on chronic left flank and low back pain following an attempted prednisone taper after a recent hospitalization. He reported that pain recurred when reducing prednisone below 60 mg and had self-managed with variable doses without relief. Initial evaluation included labs and spine imaging, which showed no acute fracture or infection, though white count was elevated consistent with steroid use or inflammation. The pain was managed with a restart of prednisone at 60 mg daily and a slow taper of 5 mg every three days, along with his baseline opioids and supportive medications. The chronic pain service recommended adding tizanidine and avoiding NSAIDs due to allergy history. Calcium, vitamin D, and Bactrim were prescribed for bone protection and infection prophylaxis given prolonged steroid use. The patient improved clinically, remained stable, and was discharged home with follow-up planned in the chronic pain clinic, while forgoing rheumatology re-engagement per his preference.

Brief Hospital Course:
SUMMARY:
========
Mr. ___ is a ___ year old man with a history of ankylosing 
spondylitis (previously treated with biologics, but discontinued 
due to infectious complications, currently managing chronic pain 
with opioids), obesity, HTN, asthma, OSA on CPAP, and multiple 
admissions for recurrent back pain, who presents with back pain. 


ACUTE ISSUES:
============= 
# Chronic pain 
Reporting severe left flank and left ""SI joint"" pain. Says these 
are classic symptoms for him. Exam notable for superficial, 
generalized tenderness to palpation over the left flank, left 
lower ribs, and lower back. No focal point tenderness or rash. 
Only mild tenderness at SI joint, with relatively stable 
CRP/ESR. Of note, patient has multiple recurrent admissions for 
pain control. Both rheumatology and chronic pain were consulted 
on admission. Both services are recommending NSAID therapy, 
muscle relaxants, and physical therapy. 

Despite these recommendations, patient is adamantly requesting 
prednisone for his symptoms. He is declining NSAIDs due to prior 
experience of, and concerns for side-effects, like bleeding. He 
declines increasing anti-spasmodic because this causes worse 
spasms in him and fatigue/sedation. He also declines ___ 
consult/evaluation. 

Otherwise, he says he is engaging in CBT which we support. Will 
also continue home opiates without change and have patient 
follow up with his PCP on discharge. At home, he is taking 
oxycodone 10 mg BID PRN + oxycontin 50 mg BID (confirmed with 
___, last filled ___ for 7 day supply). These were also 
continued during admission.

Given recurrent recent admissions for similar symptoms, we had a 
team meeting with medical team, patient, and his father prior to 
discharge. Patient expresses that he is dissatisfied with 
recommendations. However, he will call to make a follow-up with 
rheumatology to discuss further therapy with biologics as below. 
We also recommended follow up with chronic pain service as an 
outpatient if patient is amenable.

#Ankylosing spondylitis

and will call to schedule follow up in ___ clinic.
